title: Two Sum
description: You are given a list of numbers and a target value. Find the two different numbers in the list that add up to the target, and return their indices. Exactly one valid answer exists, and the same element cannot be used twice.

examples.explanation: nums[0] + nums[1] = 2 + 7 = 9, so we return their indices 0 and 1.
nums[1] + nums[2] = 2 + 4 = 6, so we return their indices 1 and 2.

hints: Think about what complement you need for each number.
A hash map can store seen values for O(1) lookup.
One pass is enough.
followUp: What if the array is sorted?

testCases.note: Minimum length array with duplicate values

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
description: You are given the price of a stock on each day. You may buy on one day and sell on a later day, completing at most one transaction. Return the maximum profit achievable, or 0 if no profit is possible.

examples.explanation: Buy on day 2 (price = 1) and sell on day 5 (price = 6), profit = 6 - 1 = 5.
Prices only go down, so no profit can be made; return 0.

hints: Track the minimum price seen so far.
At each step compute profit vs current min.
One pass is enough.

youtubeVideos.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock

relatedProblems: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II
Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock III
followUp: What if you can make multiple transactions?

testCases.note: Prices only decrease, no profit possible
Maximum possible profit at boundary values

title: Contains Duplicate
description: Given a list of numbers, determine whether any value appears more than once. Return true if a duplicate exists, otherwise return false.

examples.explanation: The number 1 appears twice in the list.
Every number in the list is different, so no duplicates exist.

hints: A hash set tracks seen elements.
Sort first, then check adjacent elements.
followUp: Can you do it in O(1) space?

title: Product of Array Except Self
description: Given a list of numbers, return a new list where each position holds the product of all the other numbers in the list except the one at that position.

examples.explanation: For index 0: 2*3*4=24, for index 1: 1*3*4=12, and so on for each position.
Because there is a single zero, every position except the zero's own position becomes 0.

constraints: The product of any prefix/suffix fits in 32-bit integer.
hints: Compute prefix products left to right.
Compute suffix products right to left.
Multiply prefix and suffix at each index.
followUp: Can you solve it with O(1) extra space (excluding output)?

testCases.note: Zero at the start of array

title: Maximum Subarray
description: Given a list of numbers, find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum, and return that sum.

examples.explanation: The subarray [4,-1,2,1] adds up to 6, which is the largest possible sum.
There is only one number, so it is itself the maximum sum subarray.

hints: Use Kadane's algorithm.
If current sum goes negative, reset to 0.
Track global max at each step.
followUp: If you have figured out the O(n) solution, try coding another solution using the divide and conquer approach.

title: Move Zeroes
description: Given a list of numbers, move all the zeroes to the end of the list while keeping the relative order of the non-zero numbers the same.

examples.explanation: Non-zero numbers 1, 3, 12 keep their original order, and both zeroes move to the end.
With only one zero in the list, there is nothing to move.

hints: Use a slow pointer for the next non-zero position.
Minimize the number of operations.
followUp: Minimize the total number of operations done.

title: Find the Duplicate Number
description: You are given a list of n+1 numbers, where every number is between 1 and n. Exactly one number is repeated, and it may appear more than twice. Find that repeated number.

examples.explanation: The number 2 appears twice in the list, so it is the duplicate.
The number 3 appears twice in the list, so it is the duplicate.

constraints: Only one duplicate, but may appear more than twice.
hints: Model it as a linked list cycle problem.
Use Floyd's cycle detection.
Don't use O(n) extra space.

youtubeVideos.title: Find the Duplicate Number - Floyd's Cycle

followUp: How about using O(1) space and O(n) time?

testCases.note: Duplicate appears in a different position
Same duplicate value repeated many times
Duplicate located at the very end

title: Intersection of Two Arrays II
description: You are given two lists of numbers. Return the numbers that appear in both lists, including each number as many times as it appears in both (based on the smaller count).

examples.explanation: The number 2 appears twice in nums1 and twice in nums2, so it appears twice in the result.
4 and 9 are common to both lists, each counted once since that's their smaller frequency.

hints: Use a frequency map for the smaller array.
Iterate the larger and decrement count.
followUp: What if the given array is already sorted?
What if one array is very large and one is small?

testCases.note: Different frequency counts in each array
Zero values with unequal duplicate counts

title: Plus One
description: A large number is represented as a list of digits, one digit per position from left to right. Add one to this number and return the resulting list of digits.

examples.explanation: The number 123 plus 1 equals 124.
The number 999 plus 1 equals 1000, which needs one extra digit.

constraints: digits does not contain leading zeros.
hints: Handle carry from the last digit.
Watch out for the all-9s edge case.
followUp: Handle arbitrary large digit arrays.

testCases.note: All 9s, result gains an extra digit
Minimum length array, single zero digit
Carry stops partway through the digits

title: Single Number
description: Every number in the list appears exactly twice, except for one number that appears only once. Find that single number.

examples.explanation: 4 is the only number that does not have a matching pair.
1 is the only number that does not have a matching pair.

constraints: Each element appears twice except one.
hints: XOR of a number with itself is 0.
XOR all elements; duplicates cancel out.
followUp: What if three elements appear once?

testCases.note: Zero handled as a valid paired value

title: Rotate Array
description: Given a list of numbers, shift every element to the right by k positions, with elements that fall off the end wrapping around to the front.

examples.explanation: Every element shifts right by 3 positions, wrapping around to the front.
Every element shifts right by 2 positions, wrapping around to the front.

hints: Reverse the full array.
Reverse first k elements.
Reverse the rest.
followUp: Try all three approaches: extra array, cyclic replacements, reversal.

testCases.note: k is greater than array length (wraps around)

title: Container With Most Water
description: You are given the heights of several vertical lines standing on the x-axis. Choose two lines that, together with the x-axis, form a container holding the most water, and return the amount of water it can hold.

examples.explanation: Choosing the lines of height 8 (index 1) and 7 (index 8) gives the largest area: 7 * 7 = 49.
There are only two lines to pick, forming an area of 1 * 1 = 1.

hints: Brute force is O(n²).
Think about using two pointers.
Move the shorter line inward.
followUp: Can you solve it in O(n)?

testCases.note: Tallest lines are at both ends
Short lines on both sides of a tall one

title: 3Sum
description: Given a list of numbers, find all the unique triplets of numbers in the list that add up to zero.

examples.explanation: These are the only two unique triplets in the list that sum to zero.
The only possible triplet is made from the three zeros, and it sums to zero.

hints: Sort the array first.
Fix one element, use two pointers for the rest.
Skip duplicates carefully.
followUp: Can you generalize to k-sum?

testCases.note: Multiple valid triplets with repeated values

title: Subarray Sum Equals K
description: Given a list of numbers and a target value k, count how many contiguous subarrays add up exactly to k.

examples.explanation: The subarrays [1,1] (first two elements) and [1,1] (last two elements) both sum to 2.
The subarrays [1,2] and [3] both sum to 3.

hints: Use prefix sums.
Store prefix sum frequencies in a hash map.
Look for prefixSum - k in the map.

youtubeVideos.title: Subarray Sum Equals K - Prefix Sum

relatedProblems: Maximum Size Subarray Sum Equals k
followUp: What if numbers are positive only — can you use sliding window?

testCases.note: Different subarray lengths give the same sum
Minimum length array, no matching subarray
Multiple zero-sum subarrays with negatives and zero

title: Sort Colors
description: You are given a list containing only the numbers 0, 1, and 2, representing three colors (red, white, blue). Rearrange the list so that all 0s come first, followed by all 1s, then all 2s.

examples.explanation: All the 0s are grouped first, followed by all the 1s, then all the 2s.
The three colors are simply arranged in order: 0, then 1, then 2.

hints: Dutch National Flag algorithm by Dijkstra.
Use three pointers: low, mid, high.
Swap elements based on mid pointer value.
followUp: One-pass algorithm using constant space.

testCases.note: Mostly one color with a single outlier

title: Maximum Product Subarray
description: Given a list of numbers, find the contiguous subarray whose numbers multiply together to give the largest product, and return that product.

examples.explanation: The subarray [2,3] gives the largest product: 2 * 3 = 6.
The subarray [-2,-1] is not continuous through index 1 (which is 0), so the best product achievable is 0.

constraints: The product of any subarray fits in 32-bit integer.
hints: Track both max and min products at each step.
Negative numbers flip max and min.
Reset on zero.
followUp: What if there are very large numbers?

testCases.note: Two negative numbers multiply into a positive result
Zero at the start of the array
Minimum length array, single negative element

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
description: A list of unique numbers, originally sorted in increasing order, has been rotated by some unknown amount. Find the smallest number in the list.

examples.explanation: The original sorted array [1,2,3,4,5] was rotated so that it starts from index 3.
The original sorted array [0,1,2,4,5,6,7] was rotated so the smallest value 0 sits in the middle.

constraints: Array is sorted and rotated between 1 and n times.
hints: Use binary search.
Compare mid with right to determine which half is sorted.
Minimum is in the unsorted half.

youtubeVideos.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array

relatedProblems: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array II
followUp: What if duplicates are allowed?

testCases.note: Minimum sits in the middle of the array

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
description: A list of unique numbers, originally sorted in increasing order, has been rotated by some unknown amount. Find the index of a given target value in the list, or return -1 if it is not present.

examples.explanation: The target value 0 is located at index 4 in the list.
The target value 3 does not exist anywhere in the list.

hints: One side of mid is always sorted.
Determine which side target falls in.
Recurse or iterate on the correct half.
relatedProblems: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
Search in Rotated Sorted Array II
followUp: What if duplicates are allowed?

testCases.note: Target not present in the list
Small rotated array, target at the start

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
description: Given an unsorted list of numbers, find the length of the longest run of consecutive numbers that can be formed using numbers from the list.

examples.explanation: The numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 form a consecutive streak of length 4.
There are no numbers in the list, so the longest streak has length 0.

hints: Put all numbers in a hash set.
Only start a sequence from a number with no predecessor.
Extend each sequence greedily.
followUp: Can you solve it in O(n) without sorting?

testCases.note: Longer consecutive streak including negative numbers

title: Jump Game
description: You start at the first position of a list, where each number represents the maximum number of steps you can jump forward from that position. Determine whether you can reach the last position.

examples.explanation: Jump 1 step from index 0 to index 1 (value 3), then jump 3 steps to reach the last index.
No matter the path taken, you always end up stuck at index 3, which has value 0.

hints: Track the farthest index reachable.
If current index exceeds max reach, return false.
followUp: What is the minimum number of jumps?

testCases.note: Minimum length array, already at the last index
Stuck immediately at the first zero

title: Spiral Matrix
description: Given a grid of numbers, return all the numbers in the order you would read them while walking around the grid in a spiral, starting from the top-left corner.

examples.explanation: Walking the outer edge first (right, down, left, up), then spiraling into the center.
The same spiral pattern applied to a rectangular (non-square) grid.

hints: Simulate direction changes with boundary variables.
Shrink top, bottom, left, right boundaries as you go.
followUp: Can you generalize to any n×m grid?

title: Trapping Rain Water
description: You are given the heights of bars forming an elevation map. If it rains, water gets trapped between the bars. Calculate the total amount of water that can be trapped.

examples.explanation: Water settles into the low spots between taller bars, adding up to 6 total units.
Water fills the dips between the tall bars on either side, totaling 9 units.

hints: Water at each index = min(maxLeft, maxRight) - height[i].
Precompute left max and right max arrays.
Or use two pointers to avoid extra space.
followUp: Can you solve it in O(1) space?

testCases.note: Minimum length array, no water can be trapped

title: First Missing Positive
description: Given an unsorted list of numbers, which may include negatives and duplicates, find the smallest positive number that is missing from the list.

examples.explanation: 1 is present in the list, but 2 is missing, so 2 is the answer.
None of the small positive numbers starting from 1 are present, so 1 is the answer.

hints: Ignore negatives and numbers > n.
Place each number at its correct index (nums[i] at index nums[i]-1).
Scan for the first index where nums[i] != i+1.
followUp: Is it possible without modifying the array?

testCases.note: No small positive numbers present at all
Minimum length array, missing number is right after
All negative numbers, smallest positive is missing

title: Sliding Window Maximum
description: You have a list of numbers and a window of fixed size k that slides across the list from left to right, one step at a time. For each position of the window, find the maximum value inside it, and return all these maximums as a list.

examples.explanation: As the window of size 3 slides across the list, the maximum in each window is recorded.
With a window size equal to the array length, the maximum is simply the single element.

hints: Use a monotonic decreasing deque.
Remove elements outside the window from the front.
Remove smaller elements from the back before inserting.
followUp: Can you solve it for a 2D matrix?

testCases.note: Minimum length array, k equals array length

title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
description: You are given the heights of bars in a histogram, each with a width of 1. Find the area of the largest rectangle that can be formed using one or more adjacent bars.

examples.explanation: The rectangle formed by the two bars of height 5 and 6 (width 2) gives an area of 10.
The tallest single bar, height 4, gives the largest rectangle area of 4.

hints: Use a monotonic increasing stack.
When a shorter bar is found, pop and compute area.
Append a 0 at the end to flush the stack.
followUp: Can you extend this to a 2D binary matrix?
